newsitem.title: CANADA: Saskatchewan harvests 46 pct of crops vs 49 pct.
newsitem.headline: Saskatchewan harvests 46 pct of crops vs 49 pct.

text.p: Saskatchewan harvested 46 percent of all crops compared to 49 percent at this time in the five-year average in the week ended Sept 16, Saskatchewan Agriculture said in its report.

Grade quality was above average for harvest spring wheat despited recent rains which reduced crop quality across the grainbelt. With 43 percent of spring wheat havested, 82 percent was expected to grade number one, 15 percent grading number two, three percent grading number three.
The 10-year average for spring wheat is 47 percent at No 1, 24 percent at No 2, 19 percent at No 3 and 10 percent feed.
Frost was reported across the province in the past week and was expected to cause some damage but the extent was not yet known. Wind damage was also reported.
Southern Saskatchewan saw an average one mm of rain. Wind and frost damage was reported on central and eastern crops.
Central Saskatchewan saw an average one mm of rain. Wind and frost damage was reported on late, immature crops. Ergot was reported around Biggar.
Northern Saskatchewan saw an average two mm of rain. Frost and wind damage was reported in the north. Ergot was reported in Hudson Bay, Tisdale, Prince Albert and Meadow Lake regions.
